title: The chat-to-deployment flow
content:
## Overview

Emergent transforms natural-language descriptions into deployed applications through a five-phase workflow. You describe what you want in chat, AI agents write and test the code, you preview the result in real time, iterate until it's right, and then deploy to production—all without leaving the platform.

This page walks through the complete arc from your first prompt to a live URL.

---

## The five phases

<Steps>

<Step title="Prompt: Describe your app">

Start a conversation in the Emergent chat interface (web or [mobile](/building-from-the-emergent-mobile-app)). Write what you want to build in plain language:

- **Simple apps**: "A to-do list with tags and due dates"
- **Data-driven tools**: "A CRM that tracks customer interactions and sends email reminders"
- **Consumer products**: "A recipe sharing app where users can save favorites and comment"

The AI agents parse your intent, ask clarifying questions if needed, and generate a technical plan. You don't need to specify frameworks, libraries, or architecture—the platform selects the stack automatically.

<Tip title="Start broad, then refine">
You'll have many chances to iterate. Begin with the core idea; worry about styling and edge cases later.
</Tip>

</Step>

<Step title="Build: Agents write, test and wire everything">

Once you confirm the plan (or the agents infer enough confidence), code generation begins:

- **Backend services** (API routes, database schemas, authentication) are scaffolded and connected.
- **Frontend UI** (React components, navigation, forms) is generated with responsive design patterns.
- **Integrations** (email, payment APIs, third-party SDKs) are wired in when requested.
- **Tests** run automatically to catch regressions before you see the preview.

The build typically completes in seconds to a few minutes, depending on app complexity. You'll see live progress in the chat and a status indicator in the [workspace](/a-tour-of-the-workspace).

</Step>

<Step title="Preview: Interact with the running app">

As soon as the build succeeds, Emergent spins up a **preview environment**—a fully functional instance of your app at a temporary URL. You can:

- Click through every screen and flow.
- Create test accounts, submit forms, trigger workflows.
- Open the preview on desktop, tablet, or phone to verify responsive behavior.

The preview environment includes live databases, auth, and any third-party integrations you've configured (using sandbox/test keys when appropriate). It's isolated from production, so you can experiment freely.

<Info>
Preview environments persist until you explicitly delete them or deploy a new version. You can share the preview URL with teammates or stakeholders for feedback.
</Info>

Learn more about the [separation between preview and deployed instances](/preview-vs-deployed-separate).

</Step>

<Step title="Iterate: Refine in natural language">

Spot a bug? Want a different layout? Return to the chat and describe the change:

- "Make the search bar sticky at the top"
- "Add a dark mode toggle in settings"
- "Fix the email validation—it's rejecting valid addresses"

The AI agents apply the edits incrementally, re-run tests, and refresh the preview. You can iterate as many times as needed. Each change is version-controlled, so you can roll back if something breaks.

<Tip title="Use screenshots and screen recordings">
Paste images or link to videos in chat to show exactly what needs fixing. The agents understand visual context.
</Tip>

</Step>

<Step title="Deploy: Push to production">

When you're satisfied with the preview, click **Deploy** in the workspace. Emergent:

1. Provisions production infrastructure (databases, storage, CDN).
2. Applies environment-specific configuration (production API keys, domain settings).
3. Runs a final test suite and security scan.
4. Deploys the app to a live, autoscaling environment.

Your app is assigned a default `*.emergent.run` URL immediately. You can [map a custom domain](/custom-domain) anytime after deployment.

<Warning title="Preview and production are separate">
Data, user accounts, and integrations in preview **do not** carry over to production. Plan your production setup (real API keys, payment processors, etc.) before the first deploy.
</Warning>

</Step>

</Steps>

---

## What happens under the hood

While you chat, Emergent's agent orchestrator:

- **Parses requirements** into discrete tasks (UI mockup, data model, API design).
- **Delegates to specialist agents** (frontend, backend, testing, deployment).
- **Runs incremental tests** after every code change to catch regressions.
- **Manages state** so context persists across conversations (you can return days later and pick up where you left off).

All code, configs, and database schemas are generated from scratch or modified in place. Nothing is templated—each app is unique.

---

## Key concepts to know

| Concept | What it means |
|---------|---------------|
| **Workspace** | The central hub where you manage builds, previews, and deployments. See [a tour of the workspace](/a-tour-of-the-workspace). |
| **Preview environment** | A temporary, fully functional instance for testing. Isolated from production. |
| **Deployed instance** | Your production app, live at a public URL with real users and data. |
| **Universal LLM Key** | A single API key that routes to multiple LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.). Required for apps that use AI features. See [the Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key). |
| **Emergent Auth** | Built-in user authentication (email/password, OAuth, magic links). No third-party auth service needed. See [Emergent Auth](/emergent-auth-built-in). |

Browse the full [glossary of Emergent terms](/glossary-of-emergent-terms) for more definitions.

---

## Mobile apps

Emergent can generate native iOS and Android apps from the same chat-based workflow. The process mirrors web:

1. Prompt for a mobile experience (or convert an existing web app with [web ↔ mobile conversion](/web-mobile-conversion-canonical)).
2. Preview in the mobile simulator or on a physical device via TestFlight / APK.
3. Iterate until ready.
4. Deploy to the App Store and Play Store (Emergent handles [build generation](/build-generation-for-a-pre-existing-play-store-app) and submission prep).

<Note>
Mobile builds take longer than web (3–10 minutes for the first compile) due to native code compilation and app store requirements.
</Note>

---

## Common first-time questions

<AccordionGroup>

<Accordion title="Do I need to write any code?">
No. Emergent generates and maintains all code. You can inspect it in the workspace editor, but editing by hand is optional—most users stay in chat.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I connect my own database or API?">
Yes. Emergent provides a managed [MongoDB database](/database-mongodb) by default, but you can connect external PostgreSQL, MySQL, Firebase, or any REST/GraphQL API via environment variables.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="How much does preview cost?">
Preview environments are free and unlimited during your trial. After that, they count toward your plan's build minutes and storage, but there's no separate preview fee.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What if I don't like the design?">
Iterate in chat. Describe the changes ("use a card layout instead of a list," "match the colors from example.com") and the agents will rebuild. You can also attach design mockups or reference screenshots.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I roll back a deployment?">
Yes. Every deployment is versioned. You can revert to any previous version from the workspace **Deployments** panel with one click.
</Accordion>

</AccordionGroup>

---

description: The big-picture arc of building on Emergent: prompt -> build -> preview -> iterate -> deploy. A map of the whole journey before diving in.
